info.name: Ping AI Demo Labs — All Collections
info.description:
Every standalone lab's API collection in one import. One top-level folder per lab, ordered as a tour:
token basics → issuance flows → delegation/actor patterns → gateway and resource-server enforcement → attack/defence → governance.

How to use it:
• Import this file, then postman/all-labs.live.environment.example.json, and select it as the environment.
• Each lab folder is self-contained: variable chaining (cookies, minted tokens) works within a folder.
• Labs with live settings (cimd, id-jag-standalone, token-workbench, mcp-resource-server, privilege-api-explorer) answer their honest
  refusal (409 pf_not_configured / needs-setup) in a bare checkout — those tests accept it. Fill real values with
  shared/postman/fill-env.mjs on the owner machine and import the filled environment for full live runs.
• Folders labelled (MOCK ONLY) target the lab's in-process simulation; no live form exists.
• Each lab's server must be running: mock-mode labs start with `docker compose up -d` in the lab repo; see the lab README.

item.name: CIBA Approval Sequence LAB
item.description:
USE CASE: CIBA out-of-band approval: an agent write held for a human approve/deny in a separate channel.

the lab's read surface (talk track, approval-sequence diagram) plus the Mock/Real toggle and its unconfigured refusal. The sequence itself is rendered from data; the lab's mock lane is a labelled simulation.

item.name: Sanity (mock, labelled)
item.description: Health and mode info (mock by default; Real is owner-run).

item.name: Story data
item.description: The talk track and the approval-sequence diagram the page renders.

item.name: Mode toggle
item.description: The Mock/Real toggle. Real needs owner-run settings (REAL_CIBA_*); without them it answers 409 with what is missing — that refusal is the negative case here.

item.name: Switch to Real without settings (negative, 409 with detail)
CIBA HITL Lab
item.description:
USE CASE: CIBA human-in-the-loop beat: a denied write returns an identifier; the human approves and the same write replays to PERMIT.

the human-in-the-loop CIBA story against in-process mocks (mock IAM, mock Authorize policy, mock CIBA, mock gateway, mock MCP/RS). A write starts the approval request, approve/deny resolve the identifier, expire expires it, decode inspects the tokens. Everything is a labelled mock; the lab has no live mode.

item.name: Sanity (mock, labelled)
item.description: Health, mode info and the scenario catalog (persona, agent, exchanger, downstream).

item.name: The CIBA beat
item.description: Write starts the approval (backchannel auth request); its identifier chains into approve, deny and expire. Expire needs a fresh identifier, so it runs last.

item.name: CIMD LAB
item.description:
USE CASE: CIMD client registration both directions: PingFederate fetching a client_id-metadata document, and the lab's own CIMD AS.

drive the lab's teaching authorization server (Direction 2), probe real PingFederate (Direction 1), and exercise the H2 2026 gateway simulation (mock only). Pair with <slug>.live.environment.json filled by shared/postman/fill-env.mjs.

item.name: Sanity
item.description: Lab liveness and configuration as the server sees it.

item.name: Direction 2 — Lab teaching AS
item.description: The lab's own CIMD-capable authorization server. Fetch its client documents and validate a pasted document. Fully local; the AS is a teaching server, not a product.

item.name: Direction 1 — Real PingFederate
item.description: The lab as a client of the real PingFederate named by PF_BASE_URL. Requires the lab server to be running with PF_BASE_URL set (Direction 1 off otherwise: requests answer 409 pf_not_configured).

item.name: H2 2026 gateway-sim (MOCK ONLY)
item.description:
Local simulation of the Ping H2 2026 claim that an MCP gateway prefers CIMD client registration. Every product claim is a Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant; no request leaves the lab.

MOCK ONLY: this lane has no live form. Requests target this lab's in-process simulation; nothing here proves anything about a customer tenant.

item.name: Delegation Lab
item.description:
USE CASE: Consent-delegated agent tokens: mint a token with an actor claim, gate tool calls on tier/actor/groups.

the consent-delegation story against in-process mocks. Read the directory (users, groups, the demo agent), mint a delegated token via consent, gate an MCP tool call with it (tier ceilings, actor allowlists, group entitlements), and browse the decision runs. The lab is a labelled simulation; there is no live mode.

item.name: Sanity (simulated, labelled)
item.description: Health, mode info, scenario catalog and the identity directory.

item.name: Consent and tool gate
item.description: Mint the delegated token (consent), then call the tool gate with it. The token object is chained into the tool call via the DELEGATED_TOKEN collection variable. Runs accumulate in /api/runs; flip a directory group or reset to change outcomes.

item.name: Tool call with the delegated token (PERMIT, Standard ceiling)
Gateway Claims LAB
item.description:
USE CASE: Gateway claim gates: act.sub/actor checks on an agent token — allow vs deny per scenario.

the measured PingFederate-style gateway claim-gate replayed with invented values. Evaluate a claim rule against a scenario token (allow, wrong act.sub, no act, act as text, wrong client), run the AgentCore governance evaluate, and read the scope-gate, posture and release notes. The gate logic follows the measurements; the values are invented and labelled.

item.name: Sanity (values invented, labelled)
item.description: Health, mode info, the scenario catalog and the posture/release notes.

item.name: Claim-gate evaluation
item.description: Evaluate by scenario id, or with a custom {token, rule}. Decision and per-claim checks come back for each; every run is recorded.

item.name: ID-JAG Standalone LAB
item.description:
USE CASE: ID-JAG end to end: RFC 8693 exchange, RFC 7523 redemption, MCP call, and the negative tests.

inspect tokens, run the playground's negative tests, and drive the live flow (issue ID-JAG by RFC 8693 exchange, redeem by RFC 7523, call the MCP server). Sign-in-gated steps need a browser sign-in session first (the pi.flow precondition folder); in Live mode the server keeps the tokens and returns decoded claims only.

item.name: Sanity
item.description: Lab liveness and backend reachability.

item.name: Inspect (no sign-in needed)
item.description: Decode and check a pasted token. Works without a session; never sends the token anywhere except the lab's own checker.

item.name: BYO inspect a pasted ID-JAG (invalid sample, negative)
pi.flow sign-in (browser-assisted precondition)
item.description: Live-mode issue/redeem/call act on the browser sign-in session's tokens. Start the sign-in in a browser at /api/id-jag-playground, complete pi.flow, then run the flow folders. These requests show the shape; they cannot replace the browser step.

item.name: Credentials POST shape (will 409 pi_flow_not_started without a browser start)
Flow (signed-in session required)
item.description: The live ID-JAG flow against the servers named in the environment: issue (RFC 8693 token exchange), redeem (RFC 7523 JWT bearer), and call the MCP server with the redeemed access token. Each answers 409 with the missing prerequisite when a step was skipped.

item.name: Negative tests catalog
item.description: The playground's negative tests, each with its expected OAuth error. GET lists them; POST runs one (needs a signed-in session and an issued ID-JAG; skipped answers pass:null with a note).

item.name: Run the replay test (skipped without a redeemed ID-JAG)
Intent PAR Inspector LAB
item.description:
USE CASE: PAR with an intent: push intent to request_uri (RFC 9126 + intent rule), negatives, and the scenario suite.

the RFC 9126 PAR endpoint with the lab's intent rule (push an intent, get a one-time request_uri), the intent-invalid negatives, the scenario suite (15 runs), and the safety scan. The authorization server is an in-process mock with a throwaway key; the lab has no live mode.

item.name: Sanity (mock, labelled)
item.description: Health, the scenario catalog and the safety scan.

item.name: PAR endpoint (RFC 9126 + intent rule)
item.description: POST /as/par with Basic client auth. The mock clients are agent-app / partner-app / legacy-web with throwaway secrets. The intent must be a JSON object with action, resource, amount, currency, subject.

item.name: Scenario suite
item.description: Run one scenario (S01..S08 ids from the catalog) or all of them at once; Reset clears the state.

item.name: MCP Gateway LAB
item.description:
USE CASE: MCP gateway policy: in-scope tool calls forward, out-of-scope deny before the backend ever runs.

the simulated MCP gateway's policy surface. Set a policy, call the third-party weather tools through the gateway (in-scope forwards, out-of-scope denies and never reach the backend), browse the decision runs, and read the scenario catalog and diagrams. The lab is a labelled simulation; there is no live mode.

item.name: Sanity (simulated, labelled)
item.description: Health, mode info (always simulated) and the scenario/diagram catalogs.

item.name: Policy
item.description: Read the active gateway policy, set one, and reset to defaults.

item.name: Tool calls through the gateway
item.description: One JSON-RPC-shaped tool call at a time. In-scope calls forward to the (mock) third-party weather server; out-of-scope calls are denied with 403 and the backend never sees them.

item.name: MCP Resource Server LAB
item.description:
USE CASE: MCP resource server auth: RFC 9728 metadata, bearer-gated JSON-RPC, 401/403 negatives.

the RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, the MCP JSON-RPC surface over POST /mcp (initialize, tools/list, tools/call) with a bearer token, and the auth negatives (no token, insufficient scope). With STRICT_AUTH=false (default) any well-formed JWT with the right aud and scope works; with STRICT_AUTH=true the token must verify against the configured PingOne issuer.

item.name: Discovery and health
item.description: Public endpoints, no token.

item.name: MCP over HTTP (bearer required)
item.description: JSON-RPC over POST /mcp. Set the SAMPLE_TOKEN collection variable (or the TOKEN environment value) to a JWT whose aud is the resource URI and whose scope covers the tool. RFC 6750: insufficient scope answers 403.

item.name: Mock Authorize LAB
item.description:
USE CASE: PingOne Authorize decisions against a mock PAP: worker token → permit/deny/indeterminate through editable rules.

the lab is itself a mock PingOne Authorize/PingFederate-shaped server. Get the mock worker token (client_credentials), call the decision endpoints directly and through the PingOne-shaped /pingone surface, read and edit the rule set, and browse the decision log. Everything is a labelled mock; the lab has no live mode.

item.name: Sanity (mock, labelled)
item.description: Health, mode info (always mock: the lab is itself the mock server) and the endpoint/rule catalog.

item.name: Worker token
item.description: The mock worker credentials, then the PingFederate-shaped token endpoint. The token is chained into the following folders via the WORKER_TOKEN collection variable.

item.name: Decisions (PingOne-shaped surface)
item.description: Decision endpoints under /pingone/api/v1/environments with the worker token, plus the direct PAP decision route that needs no token.

item.name: Rules and log
item.description: Read and reset the rule set, browse and clear the decision log.

item.name: OBO Lab
item.description:
USE CASE: On-behalf-of exchange: inbound token → actor claims → delegated token → downstream call, with leak analysis.

run the on-behalf-of exchange scenario end to end against in-process mock issuer, exchanger and downstream (inbound token, actor claims, delegated token, downstream call, delta and leak analysis), and decode the mock tokens. Everything is a labelled mock; the lab has no live mode.

item.name: Sanity (mock, labelled)
item.description: Health, mode info, and the scenario catalog (persona, agent, exchanger, downstream).

item.name: Run the OBO exchange
item.description: One run produces the whole story: inbound token, actor, delegated token, downstream call, the claim delta and the leak analysis. Decode inspects a pasted token; revoke clears state.

item.name: P1 Third-Party Exchange LAB
item.description:
USE CASE: PingOne trusting third-party-signed JWTs: token exchange per vendor profile (PF, Okta, Auth0, RFC 9068).

PingOne token exchange with third-party-signed JWTs. Run the exchange with each vendor's token profile (PingFederate, PingOne, Okta, Auth0, RFC 9068...), read the vendor comparison table and the wire/setup guides. Everything runs in-process against a labelled mock; the lab has no live mode.

item.name: Sanity (mock, labelled)
item.description: Health, mode info (always mock), the vendor catalog with its evidence, and the comparison table.

item.name: Exchange runs
item.description: One token exchange per request, with the vendor's token profile minted in-process. vendorId comes from /api/vendors (pf-cc, pf-oidc, p1, okta, auth0, rfc9068...).

item.name: Wire trace of the last run
PF Array Claims LAB
item.description:
USE CASE: Array vs string group claims at the door: exact membership vs substring accidents, both token shapes.

the PingFederate array-vs-string group-claims story at the mock MCP door. Mint tokens in both shapes (string and array groups), run the ten match scenarios (contains vs exact, decoy groups, multi-group), and read the run history. Tokens are HS256 fixtures from an in-process PingFederate stand-in, signed by a throwaway key.

item.name: Sanity
item.description: Health, mode info, the scenario catalog with expected verdicts, and the real-mode setup guide.

item.name: Mint tokens (both shapes)
item.description: Mint a token with string-shaped or array-shaped groups. The mock note says it: HS256 fixture key, signs nothing real.

item.name: Run scenarios at the door
item.description: One scenario per request; ids from the catalog. Each run records the verdict against the mock door.

item.name: Privilege API Explorer LAB
item.description:
USE CASE: Privilege console API browsing: the 447-operation catalog, connections, audit, and gated writes.

the Privilege console API surfaced for browsing — the OpenAPI operation catalog (447 ops), one operation's detail, the saved connections, the audit log, and the diagram-studio read/write diagrams. In real mode the app proxies the console with key/secret headers server-side; the mock console is mock-mode only.

item.name: Sanity
item.description: Health, mode info, the saved connections and the audit log.

item.name: Operation catalog
item.description: The Privilege console OpenAPI catalog: browse all 447 operations, filter by tag in the UI, or fetch one operation's full detail.

item.name: Diagrams
item.description: The diagram-studio read and write diagrams (the write diagram is honest about the gates).

item.name: Mock console (mock mode only) (MOCK ONLY)
item.description:
In mock mode the app serves an in-process mock console. In real mode this answers 409 mock_only — that refusal is the negative case here.

MOCK ONLY: this lane has no live form. Requests target this lab's in-process simulation; nothing here proves anything about a customer tenant.

item.name: SaaS Access LAB
item.description:
USE CASE: Zero standing access: time-boxed SaaS grants with approval routing across GitHub/Salesforce/Snowflake/etc.

the zero-standing-access story across SaaS platforms (GitHub, GitLab, Salesforce, Snowflake, Databricks, Google Workspace). Preview a time-boxed access request against the approval routing (mock mode), and read the story catalog with its platforms, roles and honest field sources. The gateway check needs live mode (real_not_available in mock — the negative case).

item.name: Sanity (mock, labelled)
item.description: Health, mode info and the story catalog: platforms with their resources and levels, the approval roles, and the honest limits.

item.name: Preview an access request (mock)
item.description: e.preview(body.request) with {mode:'mock', request:{...}}. requestedBy must be the subject or the subject's manager (an agent's custodian); resource must be one of the platform's resource ids from /api/story.

item.name: Preview a valid request (manager requests for engineer)
Preview: requester is not the manager (negative)
Gateway check (live only)
item.description: The gateway-check endpoint needs live mode with SAL_GW_URL/SAL_GW_APPS/SAL_GW_KEY_* configured; in mock it answers 409 real_not_available — the negative case here.

item.name: Session LAB
item.description:
USE CASE: PingFederate session lifetime: sign-in cookie, MFA window, app SSO, widget token, Check-Session consequences.

the PingFederate session story against in-process mocks. Sign in at the mock IdP (the cookie chains automatically in Postman/newman), authorize a redirect app, complete MFA, call an API, use the embedded widget, drop the session token and watch the Check-Session consequences, and inspect the flow reports. Every token is a labelled mock; the lab has no live mode.

item.name: Sanity (mock, labelled)
item.description: Health, mode info and the story catalog (personas and apps).

item.name: The session journey (cookie chains across requests)
item.description: Sign in creates the PingOne session cookie; authorize, complete-mfa and call-api use it (Postman/newman keep the cookie jar). The widget uses its own session token. lab/flow-reports reads the session report.

item.name: Sign in at the IdP (persona alex, pwd)
Sign in with an unknown persona (negative)
Stolen Token LAB
item.description:
USE CASE: Stolen-token attacks and defences: replay, tampering, theft across surfaces — what catches each.

run the attack-gallery scenarios against the lab's mock authorization server and gateway (bearer replay, tampering, theft across surfaces and the defences that catch them), mutate a scenario's inputs, and run the safety scan. Everything is a labelled mock; the lab has no live mode.

item.name: Sanity (mock, labelled)
item.description: Health, mode info (always mock: every token, server and gateway is in-process), and the scenario catalog.

item.name: Run scenarios
item.description: One scenario per request (S01..: ids from the catalog), all at once, and a mutation of a scenario's inputs. Reset clears the run state.

item.name: Token Workbench LAB
item.description:
USE CASE: Token inspection and conformance: decode with per-claim meaning, BCP/FAPI checker packs, tester cases.

health and metadata, mint a real client_credentials token from the configured issuer, decode and introspect tokens, run the tester case suite and the checker packs, and browse the simulated flow mechanisms.

item.name: Sanity
item.description: Lab liveness, build info and signing keys.

item.name: Mint and decode
item.description: Mint the client_credentials sample from the configured real issuer, then decode and introspect it.

item.name: Introspect the minted token at the real issuer
Tester and checker
item.description: Run the tester's full case suite against the lab's stubs, and the checker's BCP pack against the configured issuer.

item.name: Flow mechanisms (simulated) (MOCK ONLY)
item.description:
The lab's simulated OAuth/OIDC mechanism catalog and comparisons. Simulated by design: no live form exists for these.

MOCK ONLY: this lane has no live form. Requests target this lab's in-process simulation; nothing here proves anything about a customer tenant.

item.name: Trusted Issuers LAB
item.description:
USE CASE: Trusted-issuer support matrix: what each Ping surface accepts, checked per cell with mutations.

the measured trusted-issuer support matrix (PingOne, PingFederate, Advanced Identity Cloud surfaces), the per-cell token checks with mutations, and the decision guide. Every token is minted and checked in-process; the lab is a labelled simulation and has no live mode.

item.name: Sanity (simulated, labelled)
item.description: Health, build info, and the evidence-backed data sets.

item.name: Checks
item.description: Run a token check for one issuer/surface cell, with an optional mutation. Ids come from the matrix (e.g. issuer p1-env, surface p1-exchange).

item.name: WIMSE Lab
item.description:
USE CASE: WIMSE tokens: mint WIT + Txn-Token chains, validate hop binding (tth), and the attack suite.

mint WIMSE Workload Identity Tokens (wit+jwt, EdDSA) and Transaction Tokens (txn+jwt) chained from a WIT, validate the hop binding (tth), and run the attack suite (wrong aud, swapped Txn-Token, swapped WIT, expired, untrusted domain). Keys are in-process and labelled; the lab has no live mode.

item.name: Sanity
item.description: Health and build info.

item.name: Mint and hop
item.description: Mint a WIT (workloadId must be a clean wimse:// URI), chain a Txn-Token from it (sub is the end user), then validate the hop: the Txn-Token's tth must match the WIT. Both tokens chain via collection variables.

item.name: Mint a WIT with a traversal path (negative)
Mint a Txn-Token from the WIT
Attack suite
item.description: kinds: wrong-aud, swap-txn, swap-wit, expired, untrusted-domain. Each returns valid:false with the failure that caught it.

item.name: Workload Identity LAB
item.description:
USE CASE: Workload identity federation: platform-vouched token → gateway/direct MCP hops, with run evidence.

the federated-agent hop chain. Mint a federated token at the mock IdP, decode it, and call the mock MCP server both directly and through the gateway with it; the runs and netguard logs record every hop. Keys are in-process mocks (issuer .invalid); the lab has no live mode unless the owner connects a real IdP.

item.name: Sanity
item.description: Health, build info, the IdP discovery metadata and JWKS, and the diagram catalog.

item.name: Token and hops
item.description: Mint a federated token at the mock IdP (chained into the calls via the IDP_TOKEN collection variable), decode it, then call the mock MCP server direct and through the gateway. Runs and the netguard log record every hop.

variable.value: Each lab folder overrides LAB_BASE to its own port via its requests; the per-lab base is baked in the lab folder items.
